# **✍️ Quick notes**

## **Meeting Sep 1, 2026 at 21:36 SAST**

Sep 1, 2026

Meeting focused on interface improvements and pricing workflow adjustments with strategic decisions regarding project staffing and security.

## **Assessment Page UI and UX Enhancements**

* Freeze pane functionality planned for assessment page table headings to maintain visibility while scrolling.  
* Collapse functionality for headings to be added to improve user navigation.  
* Reviewer accountability field to be added to final reports.  
* Status updates to utilize icon-based indicators rather than text boxes.

## **Pricing and Risk Workflow Logic**

* Strategy to map risk variable names to human-readable text finalized.  
* System to provide real-time updates when users adjust risk ratings.  
* Table format introduced for risk identifiers, ratings, and descriptions.  
* Validation errors planned for items not priced at the needs gate.  
* Unconfirmed data fields to be bolded for clarity.  
* Save button functionality to include automatic redirection.

## **Case Memory Architecture**

* The outdated playbook feature will be removed.  
* System will utilize semantic search (RAG) for case memory retrieval.  
* Case memory retrieval restricted to relevant confirmed cover types for increased efficiency.  
* Deletion functionality for case memory approved, with an associated history log for accountability.

## **Business Strategy**

* Sashin and Cameron agreed to channel all external work opportunities through Converge AI.  
* Hiring additional development resources considered as a contingency for bandwidth constraints.

# **📝 Full notes**

Sep 1, 2026

## **Meeting Sep 1, 2026 at 21:36 SAST**

Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CqNMA_xxtirrpwKAvScoWftf_mf_b5hXt_D-TKGx0M0/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.52qadpxxe5o5) 

### **Summary**

Meeting focused on interface improvements and pricing workflow adjustments with strategic decisions regarding project staffing and security.

**Interface and workflow improvements**  
User experience upgrades include adding freeze panes, collapsible headings, and symbol-based status indicators. The pricing workflow will now trigger real-time quote recalculations when users edit risk ratings.

**System architecture and data**  
Case memory management now incorporates semantic search optimization and manual approval steps to maintain data integrity. Unpriced items will trigger error flags to prevent invalid outputs.

**Business strategy and staffing**  
The project will proceed without external collaborators due to due diligence concerns. Workload management remains flexible, prioritizing internal resources for current software development tasks.

### **Decisions**

## Aligned

* **Assessment page table headings fixed** The assessment page table headings are set to use a freeze pane effect during scrolling.

* **Collapsible headings added to assessment page** Collapsible headings are added to the assessment page to simplify navigation.

* **System flow routed to pricing page** The system flow is changed to direct users to the pricing page for review instead of the raw LLM output.

* **Pricing page made editable** The pricing page is designed to be fully editable to eliminate the need for redundant LLM API calls.

* **Risk findings displayed in table format** Risk findings are organized into a table format displaying the identifier, rating, and description.

* **Unpriced items hidden from final report** Unpriced sections are hidden from the final report view to improve clarity.

* **Confirmation items marked with bold formatting** Items requiring confirmation are styled with bold formatting for visual emphasis.

* **Navigation button 'Save and go back' added** A "save and go back" button is added to the interface workflow.

* **Accountability 'Checked by' field added** A "checked by" accountability field is added to the pricing review process.

* **Case memory search optimized** Case memory search queries are limited to specific, confirmed cover sections to improve efficiency.

* **Status updates moved to icon indicators** Text-based status updates are replaced with icon-based state indicators.

* **Case memory deletion tracking enabled** A case memory deletion function is created that requires a reason and updates a history log.

* **Third-party development work routed through Converge AI** All third-party development work will be channeled through the Converge AI business entity.

### **Details**

* **Assessment Page Improvements**: Cameron Chetty requested the addition of a "freeze pane" feature for the assessment page table headings so that section headings, such as determination and reason, remain visible while scrolling through cover types ([00:00:01](#00:00:01)).

  ![][image1]

* **CLI and SDK Demonstration**: Cameron Chetty noted that the application uses a vendor SDK and calls a single function in \`appl.py\` ([00:00:01](#00:00:01)). They and Sashin Chetty agreed to demo the software using Sashin Chetty’s screen and API key, utilizing an \`.env\` file for the setup ([00:02:16](#00:02:16)).

  ![][image2]

* **Staff Availability and Workload**: Sashin Chetty announced that they will begin a new job this Friday. While they expect the first two months to be the busiest, they stated that this role is not their priority and they are willing to quit if the workload becomes unmanageable ([00:02:16](#00:02:16)).

* **Risk Findings Interface**: To improve the user experience, Cameron Chetty and Sashin Chetty agreed to make risk findings adjustable by human users. Cameron Chetty requested the removal of variable naming on the interface, which will be replaced by a mapping to basic text, a task Sashin Chetty committed to completing ([00:03:30](#00:03:30)).

  ![][image3]

* **Collapsible Headings**: Cameron Chetty requested the addition of collapsible headings to the interface to improve usability and navigation, as the current volume of information is excessive ([00:04:30](#00:04:30)).

* **Pricing Page Workflow**: The speakers discussed streamlining the workflow, proposing that the system navigate directly to the pricing page where risks are assessed. They agreed that if a user disagrees with a risk rating, an edit feature should allow them to make amendments, triggering an immediate recalculation of the quote without returning to the initial review phase ([00:06:59](#00:06:59)).

* **Dynamic Calculation Interface**: Cameron Chetty proposed a new layout for the pricing page that utilizes a table format containing a risk identifier, rating, and short description to ensure the interface remains interactive and the calculation page updates in real-time ([00:09:04](#00:09:04)).

* **Data Validation and Pricing**: Cameron Chetty instructed that the system should only display priced items, and any required coverage section that has not been priced must trigger an error flag to prevent messy outputs ([00:10:00](#00:10:00)).

* **Base Rates and Loadings**: Sashin Chetty confirmed a base rate of 0.2%, though they need to verify this figure ([00:11:47](#00:11:47)). Cameron Chetty requested that any data points requiring confirmation be clearly marked in bold to improve visibility for the user ([00:12:49](#00:12:49)).

* **Navigation and Accountability**: Sashin Chetty agreed to implement a "save and go back" button to facilitate navigation after editing pricing ([00:12:49](#00:12:49)). To ensure accountability, they also agreed to add a field indicating which employee checked the quote ([00:14:07](#00:14:07)).

  ![][image4]

* **Playbook and Case Memory**: Sashin Chetty stated that the "playbook" feature is outdated and will be removed during the cleanup ([00:15:15](#00:15:15)). The system currently utilizes "case memory," and they discussed refining the process for how this memory is populated ([00:16:01](#00:16:01)).

* **Case Memory Optimization**: To improve efficiency, Cameron Chetty and Sashin Chetty decided that the system should only perform a semantic search for case memory after required cover sections have been confirmed, specifically targeting memory related to those confirmed cover types to avoid passing unnecessary data to the LLM ([00:16:01](#00:16:01)).

* **Status Updates UI**: Cameron Chetty requested a change to the text-based status updates, suggesting the use of symbol-based indicators with hover-over text to display details instead ([00:18:00](#00:18:00)).

* **Case Memory Management**: The speakers agreed to implement an approval step before cases are added to the memory. They also discussed adding an option to delete cases, including a reason and a history log to maintain an audit trail for deleted entries, while leaving potential restoration functionality open for future client discussion ([00:19:11](#00:19:11)).

* **External Job Offer and Business Strategy**: Sashin Chetty reported receiving an offer from an individual to work as a software engineer. The speakers agreed that if Sashin Chetty accepts, the work must be channeled through Converge AI to keep the funds within the business ([00:22:56](#00:22:56)) ([00:25:27](#00:25:27)). Sashin Chetty noted that if the workload is too high, they would consider hiring a developer named Gira ([00:27:41](#00:27:41)).

* **Business Relationship Due Diligence**: Cameron Chetty and Sashin Chetty expressed skepticism regarding the individual offering the work, noting that the person's GitHub repositories appeared to be AI-generated and uploaded simultaneously ([00:32:19](#00:32:19)). They agreed to be cautious and decided not to involve this individual in their current projects, maintaining a focus on utilizing their own resources ([00:33:11](#00:33:11)) ([00:36:43](#00:36:43)).

* **Gaming and Personal Interests**: The speakers discussed playing games such as "Dungeons of Eternity" and "Valheim," noting their progress and technical challenges with saving games on different platforms ([00:28:52](#00:28:52)) ([00:38:57](#00:38:57)).

* **Hardware and Technical Discussion**: Cameron Chetty recommended that Sashin Chetty force games to run through Apple's "Metal" graphics on their M4 MacBook for better optimization ([00:37:53](#00:37:53)). They also discussed hardware limitations, with Cameron Chetty noting their machine has 24GB of RAM and suggesting that running large LLM models locally is less efficient than using cloud hosting ([00:40:59](#00:40:59)).
